class: A retired setting still honoured on a second path to the same irreversible action
symptom: Secunetics (BambooHR), 29 September: the agent logged "SUBMITTING: pressing 'Submit Application' -- every check passed" four times -- first with State still empty, again after filling it, again after the owner solved the CAPTCHA. The form's own checks and the CAPTCHA stopped the first presses; the last one crashed because the owner had already sent it, and the application was then recorded as needing the owner although the page said 'Your application was submitted successfully'.
site: Every site (the owner's .env held the old AUTO_SUBMIT=true)
root_cause: apply_flow says there is no legacy AUTO_SUBMIT fallback and sends only through safety.evaluate_auto_submit at the hand-over, but PageAgent.submit_gate still returned 'may submit' when config.auto_submit (AUTO_SUBMIT) was on, and press_next then pressed the last Submit itself. Separately, the crash handler recorded 'needs you' without looking at what the page said.
why_tests_missed: The page-agent tests built their agent with auto_submit=True and asserted outcome 'submitted' -- they encoded the forbidden behaviour as the expected one; nothing tested that no setting lets the page agent press the last Submit.
fix: submit_gate never lets the last Submit be pressed from the page agent, whatever the settings: the last step always stops with 'ready for you to submit', which sends it to apply_flow.hand_over(), where only safety.evaluate_auto_submit may send it. A Submit on a step with more to come keeps its checks, without AUTO_SUBMIT. After an error, apply_flow.confirmed_after_all records the application as submitted when the page says it was received. The page-agent tests now expect the hand-over and submit as the owner does.
prevention: An irreversible action has exactly one code path, guarded by one decision, and a test that no setting opens another; when a setting is retired, every reader of it is removed in the same change, and tests never assert the forbidden behaviour as the expected one.
